correctness.rationale: With f(z)=sum a_k z^k, positive x_k=|a_k|^2 alpha^-k and s=alpha r^2, angular Parseval gives M_2^2=P(s) and the exact normalized radial norm yields ||f||^4=2int_0^infty P(u)^2 exp(-2u)du. Factorial moments m_j=j!/2^(j+1) form strictly log-convex ratios for each polynomial nonnegative certificate Q. For s in [n,n+1/2] take Q=u^n; for s in (n+1/2,n+1) take Q=u^n[c(n+1-s)+(s-c)u], c=n+1/2. The moment ratios place Q support at the minimum of <u^k,Q>/s^k for all k, giving <P,Q> >= <Q,Q>P(s)/Q(s); Cauchy-Schwarz then proves the sharp evaluation constant for ALL entire f with finite norm, not only polynomials. Equality requires P proportional to Q, proving full mono/two-mono classification and |B|^2/|A|^2=alpha(s-c)/[c(n+1-s)]. At s=0 constants are unique extremizers. Independent exact Fraction arithmetic checked 56 chosen certificates and 280 positive-polynomial competitor inequalities. Strict moment inequality and equality conditions give the infinite proof.
